meta.name: An AWS assistant that answers questions…

data.label: Web app
data.description: Browser chat interface. It owns private S3 assets and CloudFront access control, and shows answers with citations or an insufficient-evidence notice.

data.label: User sign-in
data.description: User pool with admin-created users, required software-token MFA, access-token scope and catalog-backed identity/region mappings.

data.label: RAG API
data.description: Bounded, authenticated HTTP API with a JWT browser route. There is no anonymous access.

data.label: Keyword retrieval + answer
data.description: Runs ACL- and region-filtered keyword retrieval, rechecks revisions so deleted or updated documents aren't cited, builds a cited answer or returns 'insufficient evidence'. It owns its execution role, logs, version and alias.

data.label: Document catalog
data.description: Stores up to 100 small UTF-8 synthetic documents with explicit ACLs and revisions. An operator ingests, updates and deletes documents through the generated management tool. Caller roles cannot write to it.

data.label: Foundation model
data.description: Existing direct foundation model, selected by a required model-ID input. Access, Converse support, quotas and regional availability are unverified.

brief.application: Build an AWS assistant that answers questions from a small synthetic document collection with source citations. Include ingestion, retrieval/indexing, model generation and an application interface. It must say when evidence is insufficient, and reflect document updates and deletions. For this first end-to-end qualification, use the approved bounded keyword-retrieval mode for at most 100 small documents; managed vector retrieval will be qualified separately. Use AWS for this synthetic qualification design. Propose Sydney as a candidate region, but do not record that as an approved deployment region. Draw the architecture and identify the next missing decision. This is a test design, not an instruction to deploy.

lastAsked.question: What kinds of documents arrive, and how many a month?
lastAsked.beginner: For example “invoices, about 3,000 a month, mostly PDF”.
lastAsked.why: It shapes the Document extraction design.

requirements.statement: When the retrieved documents do not support an answer, the assistant must say the evidence is insufficient instead of answering.
requirements.rationale: Proposed: stops the assistant from giving unsupported answers.
requirements.basis: User: "It must say when evidence is insufficient"

requirements.statement: Updated or deleted documents must be reflected in later answers; answers must never cite a deleted or outdated version.
requirements.rationale: Proposed: stale citations would undermine trust. The update delay is still to be confirmed, so no target is set yet.

requirements.statement: This qualification uses keyword retrieval over at most 100 small UTF-8 documents. Managed vector retrieval is out of scope.
requirements.rationale: Sets the scope boundary for this test, so it isn't presented as vector search.
requirements.basis: User: "bounded keyword-retrieval mode for at most 100 small documents"

decisions.subject: design.bounded-keyword-rag-on-aws-qualification-sketch
decisions.title: Bounded keyword RAG on AWS (qualification sketch)
decisions.context: Scope: synthetic qualification only, with no deployment. The web app (CloudFront + Cognito with PKCE and MFA) calls an authenticated HTTP API. The API calls a keyword-retrieval Lambda, which reads a DynamoDB catalog (up to 100 documents, with ACLs and revisions) and calls an existing Bedrock model through Converse. An operator loads documents through the generated management tool. Assumptions: Sydney (ap-southeast-2) is a candidate region only and is not approved. Model access, quotas and regional support are unverified. The model ID is still to be selected.
decisions.decision: Drawn while talking as design revision 2.
